memory_candidates.content: In neotex's extension system (lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/extensions/init.lua), manager.resync_all's bulk-reload loop calls manager.load (force=true) once per loaded extension, and each manager.load call re-invokes generate_opencode_json, which recomputes the WHOLE merged opencode.json from scratch (every currently-loaded extension's fragment) on every single step of that loop -- not just the extension being reloaded in that step. Consequence: a transient filesystem state change mid-loop (e.g. extension B's deploy file briefly missing when extension A's own reload step runs generate_opencode_json) can be observed and reported by an intermediate step even though a later step in the SAME loop self-heals it before the loop finishes, and the final on-disk file reflects the healed state. Any future aggregation or diagnostic logic built on top of this generation path must account for this per-step full-recompute behavior rather than assuming generate_opencode_json only ever sees the final, settled state.

This nvim config repo has an established convention for global, cross-repo, non-task-scoped state: a single JSON file under vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/neotex-ai/<name>.json' (see lua/neotex/plugins/ai/shared/picker/ai-tool-picker.lua's data_dir). When a new feature needs state that spans multiple projects/repos (not per-project state, which instead uses the root_state_file convention in shared/extensions/config.lua), reuse this stdpath('data')/neotex-ai convention rather than inventing a new location. To avoid a cross-repo tool recursing into the repo it is run from, compare the target directory (via vim.fn.resolve) against vim.fn.resolve(vim.fn.stdpath('config')), which identifies 'this nvim config repo' reliably when global_dir defaults are left at their standard ~/.config/nvim value.
